Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

confuse verb

bewilder, throw into confusion

also confused, confusing, I’m confused, puzzle, confusion

classical

Cic. Phil. 2.32: num conturbō tē? (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 7.2.2 (Lewis & Short)

conturbō, conturbāre, conturbāvī, conturbātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

confuse, disconcert

To throw someone’s mind into disorder; also simply “upset, worry” (Cic. Att. 7.2.2).

Other words

  • perturbō, perturbāre, perturbāvī, perturbātum — throw into confusion

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. perturbō

    Of plans, ranks, a household or a mind: to throw everything into disorder.

  • haereō, haerēre, haesī, haesum — be at a loss, be stuck

    verb, second conjugation, intransitive · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.74 (Lewis & Short)

    “I’m confused, I’m stuck” is haereō: not knowing what to say or do. Its first sense is “stick, cling”.

  • cōnfundō, cōnfundere, cōnfūdī, cōnfūsum — perplex; mix together

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Liv. 45.42.1 (Lewis & Short)

    Properly “pour together, mix” (see mix); of the mind, “perplex”, mostly after Augustus (Lewis & Short). Taking one thing for another is not cōnfundere but a mistake (see mistake).

  • cōnfūsiō animī — confusion of mind

    also used · modern · Andresian p. 36; Cic. N. D. 1.3: perturbātiō et cōnfūsiō vītae (Lewis & Short)

    A noun for the state: classically cōnfūsiō is a confounding or disorder (Cic.; Lewis & Short); Andresian adds animī.

Examples

  • num conturbō tē?

    I’m not confusing you, am I?Cic. Phil. 2.32 (Lewis & Short)

  • haerēbat nebulō: quō sē verteret, nōn habēbat

    the scoundrel was stuck: he had no idea which way to turnCic. Phil. 2.74 (Lewis & Short)

See also mix, mistake, understand.
